body.statement: Under the shifted sampling limit of \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) and the separate zero-drift critical-value limit of \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), for the explicit symmetric population \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\), the active set is \(J=\{((1,1),1),((1,1),2)\}\), both discrepancies are negative, and the rational interior design \( (\rho,\theta_1,\theta_2)=(5034/10000,25363/100000,25363/100000)\) has worst-cell power conditional on the complete both-selected event greater than \(0.86428621266\). Every admissible weight vector at \(\rho=0.02\) has worst-cell conditional power below \(0.86304573855\), and every admissible weight vector at \(\rho=0.98\) has worst-cell conditional power below \(0.86241162520\). Therefore every global maximizing holdout fraction is strictly interior.
body.justification: The certified, fully specified witness shows that the endpoint theorem has a substantive opposite regime rather than being a universal monotonicity result.
body.gap: No inspected paper gives a rigorously enclosed interior optimum for full-cell selective-randomization holdout power.
body.consumer: Designers are warned that maximizing the holdout can lose power when selector drift is weak relative to mean--rank dependence.
